question: Which infinite bases with a periodic meeting pattern (any number of knots per pair) does NAE read faithfully, with how much overlap, and what does the infinite base show that its finite repeats do not?

definitions.bounds: A pattern on a finite set extends if it extends in a finite repeat (sublattice quotient) keeping it distinct or, in two shifts, in a pattern repeating in one shift only (period 2 or 3) read exactly along the other; it does not if it fails in the window of radius R; else unsettled. One shift: the window of radius 24 is exact (de Bruijn bound).
definitions.F1: d = 1, one or two distinction kinds, one to three knot kinds, shifts {0,1,2}, connected, up to relabelling and reversal (181).
definitions.F2: d = 2, one distinction kind, one to three knot kinds, shifts {-1,0,1}^2, connected, up to the eight symmetries of Z^2 (2,247): all with one or two knot kinds (127) and a sample of 500 of the 2,120 with three (seed 20261120).
definitions.readings: states; faithful reading on sets meeting the origin unit within graph distance 2 (stopping at the first settled violation); knots per pair; for faithful patterns: some finite repeat read faithfully (F1 n = 3..15; F2 index 9..30), source labels at the first periodic state (flip inside shift 3), bonds of four for pairs two steps apart.

public_inputs.code: census.py (sha256 8722986805e2b60b639fc2b24215a684bc623a1545c6fc55b5cbea5e684d6765) beside this file; KNOTS-ALONE's knots_alone.py (its read_law_sat and connected); pysat Minisat22; 8 workers.
public_inputs.run: census.py from the repository root; output artifacts/PERIODIC-READ-20261111-001A/PERIODIC-READ-20261111-001A-E001_periodic_census/census.json and census_log.txt.

forbidden_inputs: Changing the families, sample, seeds, bounds or predictions after seeing results
primary_observable: Per family: faithful, not faithful and unsettled counts by most knots per pair; quotient comparison, source labels and bonds of four on the faithful.
cheapest_meaningful_control: F1 is exact, a check of the code; the pilot reproduced the endless six-regular weave as faithful; P1 fails on any unsettled F1 reading.

predictions.P1: Every F1 reading with states is settled.
predictions.P2: Some F2 pattern with a pair in four or more knots is read faithfully (settled).
predictions.P3: Some F2 pattern read faithfully has no finite repeat of index 9 to 30 read faithfully.
predictions.P4: In every faithful F2 pattern every pair two steps apart lies in a bond of four.

decision_rules.P2 holds: An infinite base with a pair in four knots is read natively in two shifts.
decision_rules.P2 fails: Two-shift periodic overlap read faithfully only up to three per pair in the family.
decision_rules.P3 holds: The infinite base differs from its finite repeats.

runtime: About an hour on 8 workers; registered; systemd-run --user -p MemoryMax=16G -p MemorySwapMax=0.
